problems.title: Mixed area by polarization
problems.statement_md:
Use the convention $A(K+tL)=A(K)+2tA(K,L)+t^2A(L)$ for $t\geq0$. For $C^2$ planar support functions $h,k$ with positive curvature radius, derive
$$A(K,L)=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(hk-h'k')\,d\theta.$$
Show this expression is symmetric and unchanged by translating either body.
problems.hint_md: Insert $h+tk$ into the support-function formula for area and compare the coefficient of $t$. Translation adds only first harmonics.

sources.locator: §5.1, planar specialization

problems.title: Why mixed area is monotone
problems.statement_md: For smooth strictly convex planar $L$, show that $K\subset K'$ implies $A(K,L)\leq A(K',L)$. Extend the assertion to arbitrary convex bodies by approximation; you may assume continuity of mixed area.
problems.hint_md: Integrate by parts so that $h_K$ is multiplied by the nonnegative curvature radius of $L$.

sources.locator: §5.1, monotonicity of mixed volumes

problems.title: Mixed area as a sum over polygon edges
problems.statement_md:
Let $Q$ be a convex polygon with edge lengths $\ell_i$ and outward unit normals $u_i$, and let $K$ be any planar convex body. Prove
$$2A(K,Q)=\sum_i\ell_i h_K(u_i).$$
You may use the support-measure formula $2A(K,L)=\int h_K\,dS_L$, where $S_L$ records boundary length by outward normal. Explain why translating $K$ does not change the sum.
problems.hint_md: For a polygon, the boundary-length measure has one atom per edge. The vector sum of the oriented edges vanishes.

problems.title: A segment has zero area but nonzero mixed area
problems.statement_md: Let $I$ be a segment of length $\ell$ in direction $e$, and let $b$ be the width of a planar convex body $K$ perpendicular to $e$. Prove $A(K,I)=\ell b/2$ directly from Minkowski addition. Deduce $A(I,J)=\ell m|\sin\alpha|/2$ for two segments of lengths $\ell,m$ meeting at angle $\alpha$.
problems.hint_md: Take slices parallel to the segment. Every nonempty interval gains the same length.

problems.title: Why a cutting segment cannot be discarded
problems.statement_md:
Split the radius-$r$ disk $D$ into two closed half-disks $D_+,D_-$ along a diameter $I$. Compute $A(D,D_+)$, $A(D,D_-)$ and $A(D,I)$, and verify
$$A(D,D_+)+A(D,D_-)=A(D,D)+A(D,I).$$
You may use Steiner’s formula. Explain why ignoring the zero-area intersection gives the wrong answer.
problems.hint_md: The perimeter of a half-disk includes its straight diameter. Compare coefficients in the parallel-area formula.

problems.title: When a cap can be replaced by its chord
problems.statement_md: Let $L$ be a planar convex body whose boundary contains a segment $I$ of length $\ell$ with outward normal $n$. Let $K$ be another convex body. Assume there is $x\in K$ such that, at almost every point of $\partial L\setminus I$, the outward normal belongs to the normal cone $N_K(x)=\{u:u\cdot(y-x)\leq0\text{ for every }y\in K\}$ of $K$ at $x$. Prove $A(K,L)=A(K,I)$. You may use $2A(K,L)=\int h_K\,dS_L$ and $\int u\,dS_L(u)=0$.
problems.hint_md: Translate the common supporting point to the origin. All contributions off the chord disappear.

problems.statement_md: For a planar width-$w$ body prove $A(K)+A(K,-K)=\pi w^2/2$. Compute $A(K,-K)$ for the disk and for the Reuleaux triangle. Explain why minimizing area is equivalent to maximizing reflected mixed area.
problems.hint_md: Expand the area of the difference body and use $A(-K)=A(K)$.

problems.title: The same reflected mixed area from triangle to hexagon
problems.statement_md:
Let $T$ be a centered equilateral triangle of side $w$, and set $H=\operatorname{conv}(T\cup(-T))$. For every convex $K$ with $T\subset K\subset H$, prove
$$A(K,-K)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}w^2.$$
Explain why this gives strict inclusions without a strict mixed-area inequality.
problems.hint_md: Compute the difference body of the triangle and use monotonicity at both ends of the inclusion interval.

problems.title: The skeleton and tangent polygon have the same mixed area
problems.statement_md:
Let $P$ be a nondegenerate planar Reuleaux polygon of width $w$: its boundary consists of minor radius-$w$ arcs centered at its vertices, with no redundant vertices. Let $S$ be the convex hull of the vertices. Let $C$ be the intersection of the supporting half-planes obtained from the two endpoint tangents of every arc. Prove that every convex $K$ with $S\subset K\subset C$ satisfies
$$A(K,-K)=A(S,-S)=A(P,-P)=A(C,-C).$$
Use the polygon edge formula and the fact that the normal interval of each arc is opposite to the normal cone at its center vertex.
problems.hint_md: At which directions do the support functions of $S$ and $C$ agree? Only finitely many directions enter the polygon mixed-area formula.

problems.title: The area of a skeleton’s difference body is a sine sum
problems.statement_md:
Let $P$ be a width-$w$ Reuleaux polygon with arc angles $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n$ and skeleton $S$. Prove
$$A(S+(-S))=w^2\sum_{i=1}^n\sin\theta_i.$$
You may use $\sum_i\theta_i=\pi$ and $A(S,-S)=A(P,-P)$.
problems.hint_md: Remove the circular caps from $P$, and compare the two difference-body area expansions.

problems.title: Sharp area bounds for Reuleaux skeletons
problems.statement_md:
For the skeleton $S$ of any width-$w$ Reuleaux polygon, show
$$\frac{\sqrt3}{4}w^2\leq A(S)<\frac{\pi}{4}w^2.$$
Show that the lower bound is attained only by the equilateral-triangle skeleton, and that the upper bound is a supremum approached by regular odd polygons. You may use the planar Rogers–Shephard inequality $A(S+(-S))\leq6A(S)$ and the arc constraints $0<\theta_i\leq\pi/3$, $\sum_i\theta_i=\pi$.
problems.hint_md: On $[0,\pi/3]$, bound the sine from below by its endpoint chord. For the upper bound, put the skeleton inside its Reuleaux polygon.

problems.title: Outer parallel bodies and normalization
problems.statement_md: Using planar Steiner’s formula, prove that $K+tB$ has width $w+2t$, perimeter $\pi(w+2t)$, and area $A(K)+\pi wt+\pi t^2$ when $K$ has width $w$. Show that the normalized body $(w/(w+2t))(K+tB)$ approaches a radius-$w/2$ disk as $t\to\infty$.
problems.hint_md: Adding a disk adds a constant to the support function. Examine the normalized support function as $t$ becomes large.

problems.title: A convex-hull identity from disjoint support differences
problems.statement_md:
Let $K,L$ be planar convex bodies and $H=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup L)$. Prove
$$A(H)-A(H,K)-A(H,L)+A(K,L)=0.$$
You may use the mixed-area formula $\mathcal B(f,g)=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(fg-f'g')\,d\theta$ for Lipschitz support functions, extended bilinearly to their differences. Derivatives are taken almost everywhere.
problems.hint_md: The functions $h_H-h_K$ and $h_H-h_L$ are nonnegative and cannot both be positive at the same angle.

problems.title: Area minimization becomes perimeter minus area
problems.statement_md:
For a planar width-$w$ body $K$, put $H=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup(-K))$. Prove
$$A(K,-K)=\frac w2P(H)-A(H),\qquad
A(K)=\frac{\pi w^2}{2}-\frac w2P(H)+A(H).$$
Explain why minimizing $A(K)$ is equivalent to maximizing the first right-hand side over hulls arising from width-$w$ bodies. Show that translating $K$ before taking its reflected hull changes neither objective value, although it can change the hull.
problems.hint_md: Apply the hull identity to $K,-K$ and replace their Minkowski sum by $wB$.

problems.title: A symmetric hull trapped between two concentric balls
problems.statement_md:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ have width $w$, place a circumcenter at the origin, and write $R$ for its circumradius. For $H=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup(-K))$, prove
$$h_H(u)=\frac w2+\left|h_K(u)-\frac w2\right|,\qquad
\frac w2B\subset H\subset RB.$$
Deduce $H\subset(w/\sqrt3)B$ in dimension two and $H\subset w\sqrt{3/8}\,B$ in dimension three. You may use Jung’s theorem $R\leq w\sqrt{d/(2d+2)}$.
problems.hint_md: The support of a convex hull is a maximum; opposite supports of a constant-width body sum to its width.

problems.title: Why both annulus constraints matter
problems.statement_md: For planar convex $H$, set $F(H)=P(H)/2-A(H)$. A regular hexagon between the concentric circles of radii $1/2$ and $1/\sqrt3$ has $F(H)=\sqrt3/2$. Show that deleting either constraint permits a strictly larger value: use a square if only $\tfrac12B\subset H$ is retained, and thin rectangles if only $H\subset\tfrac1{\sqrt3}B$ is retained.
problems.hint_md: Use the unit square. For the rectangles, keep every vertex on the outer circle while shrinking one side.

problems.title: A bound for centrally symmetric universal covers
problems.statement_md: A centrally symmetric convex planar set $C$ contains a congruent copy of every width-one body (the copy may depend on the body). Prove $A(C)\geq\sqrt3/2$ using mixed area. Why does this argument require central symmetry?
problems.hint_md: It is enough to put one Reuleaux triangle in the container. Central symmetry then puts its reflection there as well.

problems.title: Blaschke’s relation in three dimensions
problems.statement_md: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ have width $w$, volume $V$, and surface area $S$. Using symmetric multilinear mixed volume and $S=3V(K,K,B)$, prove $V=wS/2-\pi w^3/3$.
problems.hint_md: Introduce $a=V(K,K,-K)$. Expanding the volume of the difference body and expressing $V(K,K,wB)$ give two linear equations in $V$ and $a$.

problems.title: Three equivalent objectives in dimension three
problems.statement_md:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ have width $w$, and write $v=V(K)$, $s=\operatorname{area}(\partial K)$, $a=V(K,K,-K)$ and $b=V(B,K,-K)$, with $B$ the unit ball. Prove
$$2v+6a=\frac{4\pi w^3}{3},\qquad \frac s3+b=\frac{2\pi w^2}{3}.$$
Using Blaschke’s relation, explain why minimizing volume or surface area is equivalent to maximizing either $a$ or $b$ at fixed width.
problems.hint_md: Expand $V(K+(-K))$ and $V(B,K+(-K),K+(-K))$, using reflection invariance.

sources.locator: Equations (11)–(12), p. 11; inspected preprint dated 2 May 2024

problems.title: Lift the hull identity to three dimensions by projection
problems.statement_md:
For convex bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb R^3$, set $H=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup L)$. Prove
$$V(B,H,H)-V(B,H,K)-V(B,H,L)+V(B,K,L)=0.$$
You may use Cauchy’s projection formula $\operatorname{area}(\partial Q)=4\langle A(Q|u^\perp)\rangle$, where the brackets denote the uniform average over $u\in\mathbb S^2$, and $3V(B,Q,Q)=\operatorname{area}(\partial Q)$.
problems.hint_md: Polarize Cauchy’s formula first. Orthogonal projection commutes with convex hull and Minkowski sum.

sources.locator: Equation (14), p. 12; projection-based proof of the needed special case; inspected preprint dated 2 May 2024

problems.title: Mean width minus surface area
problems.statement_md:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ have width $w$ and let $H=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup(-K))$. Define the mean width by $M(H)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb S^2}[h_H(u)+h_H(-u)]\,d\sigma(u)$. Prove
$$3V(B,K,-K)=2\pi wM(H)-\operatorname{area}(\partial H).$$
You may use $3V(B,B,H)=\int_{\mathbb S^2}h_H\,d\sigma$. Deduce the reformulation of constant-width volume minimization as a maximization over these hulls.
problems.hint_md: Use the projected hull identity, then add the terms containing $K$ and $-K$.

sources.locator: Equations (13)–(15) and Theorem 10, p. 12; inspected preprint dated 2 May 2024

problems.title: A maximizer must touch the inner sphere
problems.statement_md:
Fix $R>w/2$. Among origin-symmetric convex bodies $H$ satisfying $(w/2)B\subset H\subset RB$, consider
$$G(H)=wV(B,B,H)-V(B,H,H).$$
Prove that every maximizer has centered inradius exactly $w/2$. Here the centered inradius is $\min_{u\in\mathbb S^2}h_H(u)$. Use homogeneity and mixed-volume monotonicity.
problems.hint_md: If the inner sphere is not touched, contract the body slightly and check the sign of the derivative.

problems.title: Why a spatial universal cover gives no positive volume bound
problems.statement_md:
Assume every width-$w$ body in $\mathbb R^3$ can be placed in an origin-symmetric convex body $D$ of volume $w^3/\sqrt2$ (the rhombic dodecahedral cover has this volume). Use mixed-volume monotonicity to derive
$$V(K)\geq\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac3{\sqrt2}\right)w^3.$$
Determine the sign and explain what this says about copying the planar covering proof.
problems.hint_md: Bound all three arguments of $V(K,K,-K)$ by the same symmetric container.

sources.locator: §4, rhombic-dodecahedron calculation, p. 11; inspected preprint dated 2 May 2024

problems.title: A volume lower bound from the inradius
problems.statement_md:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ have width $w$ and inradius $r$. Prove
$$V(K)\geq\frac{2\pi r w^3}{3(3w-2r)}.$$
You may use $3V(K)=\int_{\partial K}h_K(n)\,dS$ after translating an incenter to zero, and Blaschke’s relation. Using $r\geq w(1-\sqrt{3/8})$, deduce $V(K)\geq\frac\pi3(3\sqrt6-7)w^3$.
problems.hint_md: Every supporting plane is at distance at least $r$ from the incenter. Eliminate surface area from the resulting inequality.

sources.locator: Equation (10), p. 10; inspected preprint dated 2 May 2024

problems.title: A Meissner competitor restricts a minimizer’s inradius
problems.statement_md:
For width one, let $v_M=\pi(\tfrac23-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\arccos\tfrac13)$ be the volume of a Meissner tetrahedron. Show that any minimum-volume constant-width body must satisfy
$$1-\sqrt{3/8}\leq r\leq r_M:=\frac{9v_M}{2\pi+6v_M}.$$
Compute $r_M$ approximately. Explain why the inequalities supplied here exclude $r>r_M$, but by themselves do not exclude $r=r_M$.
problems.hint_md: A minimizer cannot have volume larger than an admissible Meissner competitor. Solve the inradius lower-bound inequality for $r$.
